findings.summary: Required fields have no visible indication, so sighted users may not know which Admin and school fields must be completed.
findings.fix: Keep the native required attributes and add visible “Required” text to those labels, or add a visible note explaining a required-field marker at the start of each affected form.
findings.evidence: Fields such as First name and School name have required attributes but no visible required marker or form-level instruction.

findings.summary: Validation errors appear only in a global alert and are not associated with the affected controls, leaving users without a direct path to correct them.
findings.fix: Render an inline text error beside each affected control, set that control's aria-invalid="true", and reference the error ID with aria-describedby; focus the first invalid control or an error summary after validation fails.
findings.evidence: The only error markup is a page-level paragraph with role="alert"; inputs have no error descriptions or invalid state.

findings.summary: The temporary-password guidance is not programmatically associated with its input, so it may be missed when users navigate directly between form controls.
findings.fix: Give the hint an ID and add that ID to the password input's aria-describedby attribute.
findings.evidence: The password hint follows the input but has no ID, and the input has no aria-describedby.

findings.summary: Deactivating an Admin takes effect on a single submit, with no confirmation or in-interface way to reverse the account status.
findings.fix: Add an accessible review-and-confirm step that identifies the Admin and offers a clear cancel action, or provide an immediate, accessible way to undo the deactivation.
findings.evidence: The row's POST form submits action=deactivate directly from a button labeled “Deactivate.”

passed: Visible text inputs, selects, textareas, and permission checkboxes have associated native labels; permission checkboxes are grouped by module with fieldset and legend.
POST actions use CSRF tokens, and the route performs server-side validation for Admin creation, permission assignments, and school configuration.
Successful updates use post/redirect/get feedback, and the stylesheet provides visible focus outlines.
notes: Static source review only; browser and assistive-technology behavior was not runtime-tested.
